title: Austin Council Fines Absent Aldermen 1883
summary:
• **Attendance Problem**: Multiple city council meetings in January 1883 were poorly attended, with numerous aldermen absent each session. The council imposed $1 fines on absent members to encourage participation.

• **Sparse Quorum**: Only 2-3 aldermen showed up to meetings, making it difficult for the council to conduct business. At least seven aldermen were regularly absent.

• **Repeated Adjournments**: Unable to accomplish much with limited attendance, the council kept rescheduling meetings, pushing business forward to the following week multiple times.

• **Enforcement Measures**: The city took a firm stance by levying fines against non-attending aldermen—an early attempt to enforce accountability on elected officials.
